helpText:
HelpThis ScreenIP Exclusions
Manage IP addresses excluded from all analytics data, and configure date-based data filtering.

Why Exclude IPs?
When you or your team visit the site, those visits show up in analytics and skew the data. Excluding your IP addresses ensures you only see real visitor activity.

Date Filter
At the top, you can enable a date filter to exclude all data before a specified date. This applies to MEMOPYK logs only (not GA4). Toggle Enable Date Filter to turn it on, then pick a start date. Useful for filtering out pre-launch test traffic.

IP Exclusion List
Below the date filter, the "IP Exclusions" section shows all excluded IPs in a table with columns: Label + IP/CIDR, User Agent, Status, Created, and Actions.

Buttons above the table:

  Show IP — Reveals your current IP address (partially masked by default for privacy).
  Exclude My IP — Detects your current IP address and adds it to the exclusion list with one click.
  Add Exclusion — Manually enter an IP address or range. You can add an optional label (e.g., "Stéphane home", "Office") to remember why it was excluded.


Per-row controls:

  Toggle switch — Enable or disable an exclusion without deleting it. Useful for temporary changes.
  Delete button (trash icon) — Permanently remove an exclusion entry.


IP Ranges
You can exclude entire networks using CIDR notation (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24 excludes all 256 addresses in that range). This is useful for office networks where many devices share a range.

Header Badge
The IPs: N badge in the analytics header shows how many IPs are currently excluded. This badge appears on all analytics tabs so you always know exclusions are active.

Tips

  Add all team members' IPs to get clean visitor data — your visits shouldn't count as real traffic
  Labels help you remember why an IP was excluded months later
  If analytics numbers suddenly jump, check if an exclusion was accidentally disabled

helpTitle: Cache Management — Video & Image Cache Control
helpText: HelpThis ScreenCache Management — Video & Image Cache ControlMEMOPYK uses server-side caching to ensure fast page loads for hero videos, gallery videos, and images. This page shows what's cached, how much storage is used, and lets you manually refresh or clear the cache when needed.Storage Management OverviewThe card at the top shows cache health at a glance:Cache Usage — Current size vs. limit (e.g., 303.9MB / 1000.0MB). The percentage badge shows how full the cache is.Auto Cleanup — Automatic expiration period (30 days). Files older than 30 days are purged automatically.Media Files — Total count of cached videos and images.Cache SectionsTwo sections show what's cached:Vidéos Hero — Critical videos for the homepage carousel, preloaded for instant display. Shows a Production badge, the cached count (e.g., 3/3), and an Update Status button to refresh status info. Each video file has a Refresh Cache button and shows its cache status (green checkmark = cached, with response time).Vidéos Galerie — Portfolio gallery videos optimized for lightbox display. Same layout: Production badge, cached count, Update Status button, and per-file Refresh Cache buttons.Each section shows: Section Status (e.g., "3/3 cached, 100%") and Performance comparison (~50ms cached vs ~1500ms uncached).Actions Globales du CacheThree buttons at the bottom for bulk operations:🚀 All Media Cache (purple) — Refreshes all media files with full verification.🧹 Smart Cleanup (blue) — Removes expired files older than 30 days and orphaned files only.🗑️ Images Orphelines (outlined) — Deletes unused images only.Below the buttons: total content count (videos + images) and total size. Recommended after each production deployment.TipsHero videos are marked Critical because the homepage loads immediately on first visit. These should always be cached.The 30-day auto cleanup prevents cache bloat. If you need longer retention, contact your administrator.If cache usage exceeds 80% (800MB), consider clearing old gallery videos that are no longer used.The cache is stored on the server filesystem, not in the database.How do I...Create a blog postStep-by-step guide to create a blog post, manually or with AI assistanceTranslate a postTranslate a post to another language using AI or manual toolsNeed more help? helpText:
HelpThis ScreenSEO Management
Configure meta tags, Open Graph data, and page-level SEO settings for the website.

Language Switcher
Use the French / English toggle in the top-right to edit SEO settings for each language separately.

Sub-Tabs

  Basic SEO - Page title, meta description, keywords, canonical URL, and a Google search result preview
  Robots - Control indexing, link following, archiving, and snippet behavior
  Social Media - Open Graph (Facebook, LinkedIn) and Twitter Card settings
  Advanced - JSON-LD structured data, hreflang alternate languages, and extra meta tags
  Live Preview - Preview the complete HTML head tags that will be generated


Actions

  Save SEO Settings - Save your changes (bottom of the form)
  History - View version history of SEO changes
  Publish - Publish current settings to the live site


Tips

  Keep titles under 70 characters and descriptions under 320 characters
  Each language version should have unique title and description
  Use the Live Preview tab to verify your tags before publishing
